findings.title: Quote author link no longer preserves the light-theme color
findings.body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the light branch of the new `dark-light-choose` expression is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. This makes embedded-post author links substantially lighter in light themes, contrary to the intended dark-theme-only substitution. Keep the primary branch at 30% and use the complementary secondary value (70%) for the dark branch.

findings.title: Mobile modal message length uses the wrong light and dark variants
findings.body: This changes a previous `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to a light branch of primary 30% and a dark branch of secondary 70%. The light-theme appearance regresses, and the dark-theme value is the inverse of the intended complementary secondary value. The light branch should remain primary 70%, with secondary 30% selected for dark themes.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading loses its intended emphasis
findings.body: The previous heading color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but this replacement uses 50% for both branches. As a result, topic-map headings become much more muted in light themes and do not receive the expected secondary 80% counterpart in dark themes. Preserve primary 20% in the light branch and use secondary 80% in the dark branch.

findings.title: Desktop group member names use a different light-theme shade
findings.body: The group-member name was previously primary at 30% lightness, but the new expression uses primary 50% in its light branch. This unnecessarily changes the light-theme styling while also selecting secondary 50% rather than the complementary secondary 70% for dark themes. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Mobile group member names use a different light-theme shade
findings.body: The old mobile group-member name color was primary at 30% lightness, but the replacement changes it to primary 50% and secondary 50%. This regresses the existing light-theme contrast and does not apply the complementary secondary 70% needed in dark themes. Preserve the primary 30% branch and use secondary 70% for the dark branch.
